title: Mailchimp API: Rate Limits and Integration Guide (2026)
summary: Mailchimp API authentication requires a unique security token to authorize data transfers. You will identify your tier's request limits to prevent errors.
body_markdown:
## Mailchimp API endpoints and resource models


Because the central gateway doesn't proxy requests between regional clusters, Mailchimp routes API requests through data centers assigned at the account level.


Every integration must parse the shard identifier from the API key to construct a valid base URL; failure to match the prefix results in a 403 Forbidden error.


> Because the central gateway doesn't proxy requests between regional clusters, Mailchimp routes API requests through data centers assigned at the account level.


### Mailchimp audience and list data model


The` /lists` resource is the primary container for all contact data. Every member has a unique identifier consisting of an MD5 hash of their lowercase email address.


Before querying or updating a subscriber, you must implement a pre-processing step, as the API doesn't accept plain-text email strings in the member-specific URI.


### How to generate the subscriber MD5 hash


To target a specific member, you must generate an MD5 hash of the email address. The API requires the email to be converted to lowercase before hashing to ensure consistency across different input sources.


If a user changes their email address, the old hash becomes invalid for future updates. You must use the new email's hash for all subsequent calls, as the` subscriber_hash` is a derived value rather than a static database ID.


In Node.js, you can generate this identifier using the native crypto module. The following snippet creates a valid hash from a standard email string.


```text
const   crypto  =    require  (  'crypto'  )  ;
const   email  =    " [email protected]  "  .  toLowerCase  (  )  ;
const   subscriberHash  =   crypto .  createHash  (  'md5'  )  .  update  (  email )  .  digest  (  'hex'  )  ;
```


Because Mailchimp treats each list as a siloed database, custom fields (known as merge tags) must be defined individually for every audience. The system doesn't support a global schema across the entire account.


### Mailchimp campaign creation and sending endpoints


Moving from a` save` state to` schedule` or` send` through distinct sub-resources, the` /campaigns` endpoint manages the lifecycle of an email.


To ensure delivery, developers must first populate the` /campaigns/{campaign_id}/content` resource, which separates the structural wrapper of the email from the actual HTML body.


This decoupling means a campaign can exist as a shell without content. A secondary validation call to the` /campaigns/{campaign_id}/actions/test` endpoint confirms that all required merge tags and footer links are present before authorizing the final broadcast.


### Mailchimp e-commerce and activity tracking endpoints


Transactional data and behavioral triggers are managed through the` /ecommerce/stores` and` /reports` resources. These link external purchase history to specific audience members.


By associating a unique` store_id` with a list, the API allows for automation triggers based on cart abandonment or lifetime value.


The structure of these calls is strictly hierarchical. Stores are the top-level entity representing your external storefront. Carts and Orders are sub-resources that track intent and completed transactions. Lines are individual items within an order that drive product-specific recommendations.


### Routing and shard identification


Correct routing depends entirely on the API key suffix.[Probecast](https://probecast.io/vendor/mailchimp) ’s analysis puts an API key ending in -us19 as an indicator that the account resides on the nineteenth US shard, requiring all calls to point to[https://us19.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/](https://us19.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/) .


An authentication failure, not a connection timeout, will result from using any other shard prefix, since credentials are valid only for your assigned shard. Once the base URL is established, the developer can begin polling the` /reports` endpoint to aggregate open and click data for specific member segments.
